title: Late Breaking Results: Fast System Technology Co-Optimization Framework for Emerging Technology Based on Graph Neural Networks
problem: Traditional technology co-optimization requires computationally expensive TCAD simulations and cell library characterization that are prohibitive for comprehensive design iterations. This challenge is amplified for emerging technologies with novel materials and device architectures.
motivation: Accelerating STCO enables faster optimization of power, performance, and area for next-generation IC design with emerging technologies.
method: The framework uses a type of AI called Graph Neural Networks—which learns patterns in interconnected data—to speed up two time-consuming parts of chip design: TCAD simulations (detailed physics-based simulations of how semiconductor devices behave) and cell library characterization (measuring how individual logic gates perform under different conditions). By using a unified model that handles both processes, the GNN approach achieves over 100X speedup at the technology simulation level, which cuts overall design iteration time by 1.9X to 14.1X across both emerging and established semiconductor technologies.
key_novelty: The core idea is using Graph Neural Networks (AI trained on patterns in interconnected data) to jointly speed up both semiconductor device simulation and logic gate characterization through a unified model.
contributions: GNN-based acceleration of TCAD simulation achieving 100X speedup over traditional methods
GNN-based cell library characterization for rapid design space exploration
Unified compact model connecting TCAD simulation and library characterization components
Demonstrated support for both emerging and traditional technologies with 1.9X-14.1X runtime improvements

metrics.speedup: 100X at technology level; 1.9X-14.1X for STCO iterations
metrics.ppa: Joint optimization of power, performance, and area
